As the nation is calling on Congress to tackle the issues that keep families up at night, Speaker Johnson is again sending the House home early for our 16th “snow day without the snow” this year. Next week will be days 17-20, and then the following week, days 21-24! Mr. Speaker, you can do better. Hardworking Americans deserve a hardworking Congress.

If Congress stayed to work, we could be:
📉 Lowering costs
🔋 Addressing AI and data centers
🛣️ Advancing Surface Transportation Reauthorization
🚜 Ensuring final passage of the Farm Bill
🏛️ Demanding accountability for Trump’s war in Iran

These companies that are developing these large language models, frontier models that are increasingly (gaining) the ability to break out and act on their own. We need to make sure that doesn’t happen.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) presents both a great opportunity for human advancement and a threat to humanity itself. Congress should work with technical experts, industry, and the public to determine what testing and oversight the most powerful systems necessitate. We can compete with China while taking seriously our responsibility to protect the safety of the American people.

For example, nuclear fission has the potential to meet our ever-expanding energy needs and the potential to wipe out life as we know it. Like with nuclear power, we need to bring the world together to create the necessary guardrails that will protect both people and the planet. Like with efforts on nuclear nonproliferation, American leadership is critical.

Congress should focus first on the most powerful systems and the risks that could cause the greatest harm. That means asking how developers test those systems before release, what safeguards keep people in control, and how serious problems should be reported and addressed. I have joined colleagues in pressing xAI about the safeguards behind its Grok chatbot; companies developing far more capable systems should face meaningful scrutiny as well.
